title: Basic MOS Device Physics
intro: Analog design treats the MOSFET as more than a switch: its second-order effects set gain, swing and speed. This chapter builds the equations every later chapter uses (Razavi, Chapter 2).

blocks.text: The plan is to derive just enough physics to get a circuit model: how the channel forms, how the drain current depends on the terminal voltages, which corrections matter (body effect, channel-length modulation, subthreshold conduction), where the capacitances come from, and the linear small-signal model used for hand analysis.

items: The MOSFET as a Device: structure, source versus drain, wells, symbols, and saturated devices as current sources.
MOS I/V Characteristics: threshold voltage, derivation of the triode and saturation equations, deep-triode resistance, regions of operation and transconductance.
Second-Order Effects: body effect, channel-length modulation, subthreshold conduction and voltage limits.
Layout and Capacitances: how a transistor is drawn, junction and overlap capacitances, and how the gate capacitances change between regions.
MOS Device Models: the small-signal model ($g_m$, $g_{mb}$, $r_o$, capacitances), the PMOS model, Level 1 SPICE parameters, NMOS versus PMOS and long versus short channel.
FinFETs and the MOS Capacitor: the three-dimensional transistor of recent nodes and the capacitance-voltage curve of a MOS structure.

blocks.tex: r_o \approx \frac{1}{\lambda I_D}, \qquad g_{mb} = \eta\, g_m = \frac{\gamma}{2\sqrt{2\Phi_F + V_{SB}}}\, g_m

blocks.text: Throughout, NMOS quantities are written as positive numbers. For a PMOS the same equations hold with $\mu_p$ and all voltages and currents reversed in sign, or equivalently with $V_{SG}$, $V_{SD}$ and $|V_{TH}|$.

blocks.title: A first sizing
blocks.text: An NMOS must give $g_m = 1\text{ mS}$ at $I_D = 100\,\mu\text{A}$ in a process with $\mu_n C_{ox} = 300\,\mu\text{A/V}^2$. Find the overdrive and $W/L$. If $\lambda = 0.15\text{ V}^{-1}$ at the chosen length, what is the intrinsic gain $g_m r_o$?
blocks.hint: Use the $2I_D/V_{ov}$ form first, then the square law for $W/L$.
solution: From the square law, $W/L = \frac{2 I_D}{\mu_n C_{ox} V_{ov}^2} = \frac{200\,\mu\text{A}}{300\,\mu\text{A/V}^2 \cdot 0.04\text{ V}^2} \approx 16.7$.
$r_o = 1/(\lambda I_D) = 66.7\text{ k}\Omega$, so $g_m r_o = 66.7$ (the same as $2/(\lambda V_{ov})$).
